title: The Five Oceans
keyIdea: Earth has five named oceans — Pacific (largest), Atlantic, Indian, Southern, and Arctic (smallest and coldest) — that form one connected global ocean.
familyTip: On a world map, point to each ocean by name. Ask which is biggest and which is near the North Pole.

visual.caption: Ocean fact or mix-up? Drag each clue, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: map five oceans, name them, largest and coldest, connect, challenge.

kid: Earth has five big oceans with names.
Their names are Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern, and Arctic.
Pacific is the biggest. Arctic is the smallest and the coldest.
The five names are parts of one big ocean that joins up.
adult: KS2 geography: five ocean names for one global ocean. Words: Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern, Arctic.
Common mistake: thinking walls seal oceans apart, or calling Arctic the biggest, or mixing oceans with ponds.
In the lab your child finds five spots on a map, picks Pacific as biggest and Arctic as coldest, and sees they join.
